title: "GMM Clustering of Combination AUCs"
author:
  - "**[Editor]** ZCode (GLM) — AI-generated, independently AI-reviewed;"
---

After exhaustively screening 2^k - 1 gene-combination models, the reference clusters the (model index, AUC) scatter with a **Gaussian mixture model (GMM)** to separate the "useless model" mass from the "high-AUC tail" - the optimal combination comes from the highest-AUC cluster \[1\]. `mclust::Mclust()` does the clustering; this tutorial simulates 1023 model AUCs with a planted tail and reproduces the classified scatter:

## Example

![](../images/Distribution/GmmClusterPlot_demo.png){fig-alt="GMM Clustering of Combination AUCs DEMO" fig-align="center" width="60%"}

## Setup

-   System Requirements: Cross-platform (Linux/MacOS/Windows)

-   Programming language: R

-   Dependent packages: `mclust`

```{r packages setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, output=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(mclust)
})
```

```{r}
sessioninfo::session_info("attached")
```

## Data Preparation

1023 simulated combination AUCs: a large Gaussian lobe around 0.55 plus an increasing tail up to ~0.72 (the planted high-AUC cluster GMM must isolate):

```{r load data}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(mclust))
set.seed(21901)
n_models <- 1023
aucDF <- data.frame(
  model = 1:n_models,
  auc = c(rnorm(700, 0.55, 0.04), rnorm(200, 0.60, 0.03),
          rnorm(100, 0.66, 0.02), rnorm(23, 0.71, 0.01)))
```

## Visualization

### 1. GMM-Classified AUC Scatter

`Mclust(aucDF[, c("model", "auc")])` with default BIC model selection: points coloured by GMM cluster, the high-AUC tail separated from the useless-model mass:

```{r}
#| label: fig-1.1GmmCluster
#| fig-cap: "GMM clustering of 1023 simulated combination-model AUCs over model index: points coloured by Gaussian-mixture cluster (BIC-selected), separating the useless-model mass from the high-AUC tail."
#| out.width: "85%"
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5

mod <- Mclust(aucDF[, c("model", "auc")])
plot(mod, what = "classification")
abline(h = 0.71, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
```

::: callout-tip
**Practice tips**

-   `Mclust()` with no explicit `G` uses BIC to select both the number of clusters (1-9) and the covariance model.
-   The best combination comes from the **highest-AUC cluster**, not the global maximum.
-   With 1023 combinations and a median-split + log-rank, the winning P is maximally selected - validate independently.
:::
